text:
maria: quick follow-up from RFC: we prototyped 'credit fencing' + sandboxing to isolate bursty tenants. want feedback on the planned penalty handshake and telemetry before we file the rollout playbook

ajay: tl;dr pls — what are the hotspots?

maria: two main pieces: 1) tethering per-tenant soft credits to a sandbox pool that caps effective concurrency, 2) an adaptive penalty window when abuse signals (spike+high token churn) trip. goal: reduce noisy neighbors without hard evictions

jeff: sounds sensible. how do we keep latency SLOs predictable for steady tenants during a surge?

maria: steady tenants get a baseline reserved credit; sandbox only takes from burst budget. if global contention, routing policy moves low-priority bursts to slower model variants or regional spare capacity

lina: concern: admission surface — do we enforce fencing at the edge proxy or central admission service? tradeoffs?

ajay: edge enforcement is faster for per-request decisioning but proliferates state. central gives single truth for accounting and easier global backpressure. maybe hybrid: edge coarsely enforces (fast token checks), central reconciles and issues penalty windows

maria: exactly our current thinking. edge keeps a leaky-bucket for immediate gating + telemetry, central runs a reconciliation job that adjusts per-tenant shadow-penalties and issues short-lived soft tokens

jeff: penalty window behavior? linear decay or backoff multiplier?

maria: proposal: two-mode decay: short aggressive backoff for compact abuse bursts (e.g., multiplier 0.2 for 30s) + long gentle taper (linear release over 10m) to avoid oscillation across shards

lina: need to be careful with oscillation across routing boundaries — if penalty only updates central, some edge proxies may still accept bursts until reconciliation lands

ajay: can add a fast invalidation path: central publishes small invalidation deltas via pubsub. edges subscribe and apply immediate caps; then full reconciliation follows asynchronously

jeff: telemetry requirements? we'll need per-tenant P50/P95 latency, token churn rate, prefix hit ratio (cache), rejection rate, and a signal for 'burstiness' defined as short-window >X qps and >Y tokens/sec

maria: agreed. also want a composite abuse_score so downstream policies can tie into cost-of-fallback (like switch to smaller model)

infra-bot: perf-test results uploaded: https://ci.company/perm/credit-fence/experiment-42 — 5% P95 regression on noisy neighbor baseline, but 27% reduction in cross-tenant tail impact

lina: re: rollout: prefer canary on Dedicated first (fix infra churn) then 10% hosted, observe degradation metrics and false positive rate on admissions

ajay: what about developer UX: how do we surface soft-penalties? API responses should include structured fields, not just 429s

maria: plan: structured response {"admit": "soft", "penalty": "0.2", "reason": "burst_fence"} in JSON + headers with retry-after estimate. also console traces and per-route telemetry in Redwood Console

jeff: backwards compatibility: some SDKs expect single 429 code. We should keep a graceful fallback to 429 for older clients but attach a new header X-Redwood-Penalty for observability

lina: testing matrix: simulate multi-tenant bursts, varying model sizes, cold kv-cache hit rates. Also test cross-region routing where spare capacity exists but needs fallbacks

maria: ops playbook draft: steps to rollback, quick disable flags (edge gating off), central reconciliation pause, and a script to reflatten penalty windows. I'll add runbook snippets

ajay: one more: are we throttling at token granularity or request-concurrency? some abuse patterns are long-running chats with low concurrency but huge token churn

maria: both. admission uses a composite budget: concurrency slots + token tokens/sec budget. abuse_score accounts for both velocity and total tokens over a sliding window

jeff: sounds good. let's add a short RFC appendix on the exact scoring function so product folks can reason about false positives

maria: will do. I'll update the repo with design + telemetry dashboards and link here when ready

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-1342: "credit-fencing rollout + telemetry dashboard"

lina: thanks — ping when the dashboard link is live and we'll schedule a canary window

maria: thanks all, especially for the edge-vs-central tradeoffs. next: we should sync with security on signal thresholds to avoid unexpected legal/retention pitfalls

ajay: can we put the reconciliation interval and invalidation pubsub contract in the PR? rough numbers: pubsub delta under 200ms, full reconciliation every 5s for critical tenants

maria: noted. draft PR will include those numbers and a small simulator. posting PR in ~2 days

jeff: :thumbsup:

lina: :heart:

maria: end of thread — will post updates here
